officialLinks.label: Authorized undergraduate and graduate grading symbols
Academic standing and repeated failed courses

helpIntro: Princeton does not officially compute or certify GPA, but the Registrar publishes a 4.0 conversion for applications. Enter semester hours and final grades to create a planning estimate.
helpNote: For current undergraduate records (2000-01 onward). A+ = 4.0; P, AUD, Inc, W and transfer credit are excluded. Repeat Impact is unavailable because a repeated course does not erase the original grade.
helpExample: A regular 4-hour A earns 16 points and a regular 4-hour B+ earns 13.2. Together, 29.2 ÷ 8 = 3.65.

gradeExplanations.D: D = 1.0 and is normally the minimum passing grade.
gradeExplanations.F: F = 0.0 and remains part of the record.
gradeExplanations.P: Pass is excluded from the Registrar GPA conversion.
gradeExplanations.AUD: Audit is excluded from the Registrar GPA conversion.
gradeExplanations.Inc: Incomplete is excluded until replaced by a final grade.
gradeExplanations.W: Withdrawal is excluded from the Registrar GPA conversion.
gradeExplanations.T: Transfer credit is excluded from the Princeton GPA conversion.
gradeExplanations.YR: Year-long first-term notation; use the final grade when the course is completed.

specialTypes.name: Princeton course / independent work
specialTypes.note: Enter the semester hours assigned by the Registrar conversion: regular courses are generally 4; thesis and specified courses may be 8.

specialTypes.name: Approved transfer credit
specialTypes.note: Approved outside credit appears as transfer credit and does not factor into the Princeton GPA conversion.

specialTypes.name: Study abroad / host-university course
specialTypes.note: Most host-university grades do not appear on the Princeton transcript or enter the departmental GPA; Princeton-taught exceptions should be entered as Princeton courses.

specialTypes.name: Pre-2000-01 Princeton record
specialTypes.note: A+ used 4.3 before 2000-01. Use the Registrar guidance or transcript-specific review for historical records.

specialTypes.name: Graduate record
specialTypes.note: Graduate grading and program progress rules differ; this undergraduate planning profile should not be used as an official graduate GPA.

repeatPolicy.note: Enter both graded attempts as separate completed courses. Repeat Impact is disabled because Princeton does not replace the original grade in this planning calculation.
